listing_view.reasoning: Subscription built to ~70x by close (69.5x at 13:02 on closing day), which signals strong demand and a likely listing pop, though the heaviest bids arrive at the end in Indian IPOs and this number includes leverage-driven NIIs. The pricing at ₹632 implies P/E of ~36 against the seller's own hand-picked peer median of 103, leaving apparent headroom that a demand-hungry market will chase on listing day.

longterm_view.reasoning: Growth is real and returns are high (ROCE 70%), but the P&L is not converting to cash: operating cash flow was ₹258m against ₹1,804m EBITDA (conversion 0.14), and receivable days sit at ~118. Top 10 customers supply 93-95% of revenue for three straight years [business, page 246], so margins and that 70% ROCE rest on a handful of buyers and a raw-material market the document itself calls increasingly competitive [business, page 256].

governance.reasoning: The extracts show boilerplate no-conflict statements and a reference to ongoing related-party transactions disclosed at Note 40 [promoters, page 311][related_party, page 414], plus a flagged resignation from a promoter-group trust [promoters, page 311] — nothing disqualifying in what I was given, but 'no conflict' asserted by the seller is weak evidence.

key_risks.why_it_matters: 93-95% of revenue from top 10 customers for three consecutive years means losing one buyer could collapse the growth story the valuation depends on.
Operating cash flow is a fraction of EBITDA (0.14x) and was negative in Fiscal 2024, so reported earnings quality is poor and the working-capital build consumes the fresh capital.
The prospectus itself flags heightened competition for critical raw materials, which threatens the margin expansion (11% to 28% EBITDA margin) that drives the P/E case.
Customers pay in ~118 days, so every incremental rupee of the 45% revenue growth must be funded upfront, worsening the cash gap as the company scales.

answers.question: is the peer set fairly chosen, and are the peers themselves expensive rather than this being cheap?
answers.answer: The 103x benchmark is inflated by the seller's choices: Hitachi Energy (159x), Schneider (155x), CG Power (115x) are expensive large-caps; the closest peer, Transformers & Rectifiers, trades at 32x — BELOW this IPO's 36x. So Kanohar is not 'cheap vs peers'; it is priced above its most comparable listed competitor and the discount is manufactured by the peer selection. Against a fair comparator it is fully or over-priced.

answers.question: check receivables and inventory against the sales growth
answers.answer: Receivable days actually IMPROVED from 158 to 118 days while revenue grew 45% in the latest year, so receivables are not obviously being stuffed to manufacture sales — but ~118 days is still long in absolute terms and OCF of ₹258m vs ₹1,804m EBITDA shows the growth is consuming cash. No inventory figure was provided to me, so inventory cannot be checked from what I was given.

answer.what_would_change_my_mind: Evidence that the cash conversion problem is timing (e.g., order-book receipts scheduled post-Fiscal 2026) rather than structural, or disclosure of diversified customer additions, would lift the long-term view; conversely, inventory build data or related-party sales within the top 10 customers would push me lower.
